title: Atomic and Nuclear Mass Spectra as Harmonic Solutions of a Common Standing-Wave Closure Condition
content: A standing-wave closure condition in Delta-c Mechanics has two lowest exact orbital solutions: a closed full-orbit branch and an open half-orbit branch. These define, respectively, the atomic and nuclear kernels and satisfy the reciprocal relation α K_A K_N = 1. The principal result is the existence, within the proposed two-photon dynamics, of a single standing-wave closure condition whose two lowest branches correspond to the atomic and nuclear domains. The particle-mass relations that follow are presented as quantitative tests of this structural correspondence, not as an independent derivation of the mass spectrum; a unique, mass-independent generation rule for all higher harmonic assignments remains an open problem, stated as such in Appendix F. The reflecting interior boundary selects even Fourier modes and half-contour phase-lock conditions; multi-flow kernel products then determine rest-mass ratios through the binding law m_x/m_e = √E_x. The proton defines the three-flow nuclear ground state and is disclosed as the calibration identity for the anomalous nuclear ratio η. Independent tests include the neutron (0.268 ppm raw discrepancy), the charged pion (1.5σ from PDG 2024), the muon (−4.1 ppm raw), the tauon (within present uncertainty with a stated higher-harmonic prediction), and the top quark (within its 0.4 GeV measurement uncertainty). The purpose is not to replace QCD or electroweak theory in this paper, but to test whether one harmonic closure structure displays quantitative consilience from hydrogen spectroscopy to the nuclear mass scale.
